# PR #3640: Patch: no flaky checks on main: the duos clock tests and two web unit timeouts

Closes #3564

## What changed

This is test code only, in three files. No production code, spec or patch fragment changed. `classify` says `Internal`.

**`crates/server/tests/actor/duos.rs`**
- **`duos_with` takes a seed.** It gains a `seed: Option<&str>`, which goes into the room-create body. The test app runs in end-to-end mode, which is the only mode that accepts a room's seed (R143). The three callers that keep a random deal pass `None`.
- **R268 (the mulligan clock test) was never a clock race.** The old check read each person's hand from the first round-1 view. But the last mulligan answer opens round 1 in the same reduce, so turn 1 has already run when that view goes out, and turn 1's draws can legally move a kept card out of the hand. The test now:
  - plays the pinned deal `R268_SEED = "seed-r268"`;
  - checks that each person's logged mulligan keeps exactly the cards dealt, compared as sorted lists of ids. The old log check only compared counts.
- **B36 (the AI team's round test)** plays the pinned deal `B36_SEED = "seed-b36"`. Its two `expect`s now panic with `last_view(&a1)`, so a failure in CI shows the round, the result and what was offered. That is the host's own seat view, so it shows nothing hidden.

**`apps/web/src/cards/art/scene.test.ts`**: a new named constant `SWEEP_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`, passed to the two sweeps over every kit part and every seed. They are heavy by design, and one ran 5,027 ms in CI.

**`apps/web/src/wording.test.ts`**: the `beforeAll` that parses the whole client now takes the file's existing `SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS`. The scans already had their own timeout, but the hook still ran under vitest's default 10 s for a hook, which the parse is growing toward. I updated the constant's doc comment to say this.

## Evidence

**R268 is not a race (checked in this run).** I put the old hand check back for a moment and ran it on the planner's two failing seeds:
- `6497a41d6a67dc1b98dee644c48a53b3` fails with `A2 keeps c9: dealt ["c3", "c9", "c8"], holds ["c3", "c8", "c17", "c11", "c19"]`.

- `seed-r268` passes.

The new check passes on both bad seeds, and the committed file holds `seed-r268`. The planner traced the first seed: A2 draws a Cognitive Offloading on turn 1, the autopilot plays A2's turn, and it summons the EU Striker A2 had kept. My run shows the same thing from outside: c9 left A2's hand while A2 held three new cards.

**B36's failure in CI (310f441) was not reproduced.**
- The planner saw 0 failures in 2,700 random-seed runs.
- I checked that tokio 1.53.2 stops the paused clock from moving while a `spawn_blocking` task runs (`runtime/blocking/schedule.rs` calls `inhibit_auto_advance`). So a slow AI search on a busy runner cannot use up the round clock in paused time.
- The AI's search still stops on the wall clock (`BOT_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS`), so a starved runner can play a different game from the same seed. If it fails again, the new panic message shows where it stood.
